why: Quote is verbatim (python.md:1665, whole line reads '* `is_error`: `True` when the conversation ended in an error state. Always `True` on the `error_*` subtypes. On `subtype="success"` it is `True` when the final model request failed, meaning the agent loop completed but the last API call returned an error.'), and the IDENTIFIER half of the finding is true: adaptResult (event-adapter.ts:578-585) derives terminalReason from stop_reason + subtype only, and grep -a shows no read of is_error, api_error_status or terminal_reason anywhere on the Claude result path. But the CONSEQUENCE is false, which is exactly this repo's recurring false-positive shape: something one layer up already handled it. Disassembling the shipped CLI (node_modules/@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk-darwin-arm64/claude) shows the success-result emitter derives BOTH flags from the last assistant message and nothing else: `if(vs.type==="assistant"){ ... Eo=Boolean(vs.isApiErrorMessage), wr=vs.apiErrorStatus??null }` then `yield{type:"result",subtype:"success",is_error:Eo,api_error_status:wr,...}`. That assistant message is built exclusively by the factory `tc({content,apiError,error,errorDetails})`, which sets `isApiErrorMessage:!0` AND `error:<SDKAssistantMessageError>`; `nRn` then stamps `r.apiErrorStatus=e.status`. Every one of the 44 `return tc({...})` branches supplies an error code (a 529 lands in `if(e instanceof es && e.status>=500)` -> `error:"server_error"`; the terminal fallbacks use `error:"unknown"`). The wire serializer `function*Fct` forwards it unconditionally: `yield{type:"assistant",message:r.message,parent_tool_use_id:null,session_id:kt(),uuid:r.uuid,error:r.error,...}`. So the very message that makes is_error true and carries api_error_status arrives at our adapter one message BEFORE the result, with `error` set, and adaptAssistant (event-adapter.ts:294-300) intercepts it first -- `if ('error' in message && message.error) { events.push(await this.callbacks.mapSDKError(...)); return; }` -- yielding a typed_error built by mapClaudeSdkAssistantError (claude-agent.ts:2660-2675, claude-sdk-error-mapper.ts:210). Covered by an existing test: claude-event-adapter.test.ts:231 'should handle SDK errors via callback' asserts assistant {error:'rate_limit'} -> typed_error. A 529 turn is therefore NOT 'indistinguishable from a clean success' and NOT emitted with 'no error event'. Not an inert-worklist section 3 owner decision (none of the nine touch this) and not a deliberate fork difference.
correctedState: Partially true but the stated consequence is wrong. TRUE: adaptResult (packages/shared/src/agent/backend/claude/event-adapter.ts:578-585) reads only stop_reason and subtype, so an api-error success result gets terminalReason undefined, and neither is_error, api_error_status nor terminal_reason is read anywhere on the Claude path. FALSE: that the turn is indistinguishable from a clean success. The shipped CLI sets is_error/api_error_status on a success result solely from the last assistant message's isApiErrorMessage/apiErrorStatus, and that same message is emitted on the wire with error:<SDKAssistantMessageError> ('server_error' for a 529 via the status>=500 branch); adaptAssistant intercepts it at event-adapter.ts:294-300 and pushes a typed_error via mapClaudeSdkAssistantError before the result ever arrives. The real residual gap is narrower and cosmetic-to-diagnostic: we lose the numeric HTTP status (api_error_status) and the complete event carries no terminalReason ('api_error') for that turn, so an api-error completion is labelled 'complete' alongside a user-visible typed_error rather than being marked terminal. Worth an enrichment (read api_error_status into the typed_error details and map terminal_reason==='api_error' onto terminalReason), not an error-surfacing fix.
